items.title: Wisconsin’s Roller Coaster of a Democratic Primary Race for Governor Crashes to an End
items.author: Jess Bidgood
items.content: <article>Democrats appear likely to nominate a democratic socialist for governor. How did they get here?</article>

items.title: Sanders Calls on A.I. Companies to Pause Development to ‘Avoid Disaster’
items.author: Lisa Lerer
items.content: <article>Senator Bernie Sanders warned that corporations have already lost control of technology that could cause “potentially cataclysmic results” for millions of people.</article>

items.title: D.C.-Area Airport to Close for 3 Hours for Grand Prix Event
items.author: Karoun Demirjian
items.content: <article>The Federal Aviation Administration has imposed other closures at Reagan National Airport over events for the 250th anniversary of the nation’s founding.</article>

items.title: Ben Jones, ‘Dukes of Hazzard’ Actor and Congressman, Dies at 84
items.author: Glenn Rifkin
items.content: <article>He played the mechanic Cooter Davenport on the hit television series before serving two terms as a Democratic congressman from Georgia.</article>

items.title: Hegseth Renames Base for Lindsey Graham
items.author: John Ismay
items.content: <article>Joint Base Charleston will now be known as Joint Base Lindsey Graham. The senator served as a judge advocate general before retiring as a colonel in 2015.</article>

items.title: Trump Concedes There Was ‘Some Contractor Error’ in Reflecting Pool Renovations
items.author: David A. Fahrenthold
items.content: <article>The president had insisted for weeks that the landmarks’ algae-stained waters and peeling lining were the fault of vandals, not the project itself.</article>

items.title: Trump Shrugs Off A.I. and Data Center Concerns as Voters Grow Anxious
items.author: Tony Romm
items.content: <article>The president and his top aides have been especially bullish about data centers, despite national blowback against the facilities.</article>

items.title: Minnesota’s Democratic Senate Primary Pits Angie Craig Against Peggy Flanagan
items.author: Ernesto Londoño and Tim Balk
items.content: <article>The Senate primary race in Minnesota will be the latest test of left-wing energy in the party, in a state that was convulsed by the Trump administration’s deadly immigration crackdown this winter.</article>

items.title: The Campaign Tactics Helping Progressives Win Primaries Ahead of the 2026 Midterms
items.author: Kellen Browning, Tim Balk and Dan Simmons
items.content: <article>Progressives are being outspent and are receiving little support from the Democratic Party. Their tactics show a different way to succeed.</article>

items.title: Obama and Abdul El-Sayed Discuss Unity After Michigan Senate Primary
items.author: Tim Balk and Bayliss Wagner
items.content: <article>Dr. Abdul El-Sayed’s call with the former president comes as he tries to win over wary Democrats in Michigan’s high-stakes Senate race.</article>

items.title: Trump Names Will Scharf as White House Counsel
items.author: Maggie Haberman
items.content: <article>The president said Mr. Scharf, a deeply conservative lawyer and the current staff secretary, would replace David Warrington in early September.</article>

items.title: Michigan Senate Candidate, a Former Trump Critic, Shifts Toward Election Skepticism
items.author: Beth Reinhard
items.content: <article>Mike Rogers, the Republican nominee, has suggested that further scrutiny of the 2020 election was warranted and that voting irregularities sank his first Senate bid two years ago.</article>

items.title: A Democratic Socialist Seeks New Voters in an Unlikely Place: Fox News
items.author: Jeremy W. Peters
items.content: <article>Gustavo Gordillo, a leader of the New York D.S.A., wants to reach new voters. But in interviews with conservative media, the backlash can be sharp.</article>

items.title: Trump Crypto Took $100 Million From a Businessman With Red Flags
items.author: Russ Buettner
items.content: <article>The curious case of Guren “Bobby” Zhou shows the ease with which investors with shady backgrounds and unknown motivations can funnel money to the president.</article>

items.title: The Lonely Crew at the Kennedy Center Will Miss Its…Mice
items.author: Elizabeth Williamson
items.content: <article>Employees say the performing arts center’s quirky-looking mice have an exotic back story. Do they?</article>

items.title: A Democrat Sounds the Alarm on Christian Nationalism in Congress
items.author: Annie Karni
items.content: <article>Representative Jared Huffman of California, the only self-declared “humanist” in Congress, writes in a new book that the separation of church and state is in grave danger.</article>
